Limit dosages and durations to the minimum required and monitor closely for signs of respiratory depression and sedation. 46. Nabilone and Zuranolone: Co-administration may increase psychomotor impairment or CNS depressant effects. Avoid concurrent use or consider dose reduction if unavoidable. 47. General Warnings: Nabilone may cause tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, and psychotropic effects when combined with alcohol or other psychoactive substances. It may impair the ability to drive or perform hazardous tasks. It is not recommended during lactation and is classified as Pregnancy Category C. Use only in patients for whom conventional antiemetics have failed. This information highlights the importance of careful monitoring and individualized patient care when prescribing nabilone, especially in combination with other medications.
